proposals.rule: When an input port is wider than 32 bits, explicitly test values that exercise the full range of its index bits (e.g., all zeros, all ones, and a pattern that increments/decrements across the width).
proposals.summary: Add a rule to stimulate wide inputs with edge‑case index patterns.
proposals.reasoning: The missed designs (Prob021_mux256to1v, Prob054_edgedetect, Prob080_timer) all involve wide inputs where the bug manifests only when selection/index values exercise the extreme or wrap‑around cases. Adding a rule that forces the attacker to consider full‑range index values will increase the chance of hitting those corner cases.

proposals.summary: Add a static analysis tool that flags designs where shift or index expressions could exceed the width of an input port.
proposals.reasoning: Several missed bugs stem from index calculations (e.g., sel << 2) that can overflow the input width when the selector reaches its maximum. A tool that statically detects such potential overflows will give the attacker hints to generate stimuli targeting those conditions.

proposals.summary: Double the maximum allowed cycles for stimulus generation.
proposals.reasoning: Many missed designs required longer sequences to reveal the bug (e.g., Prob080_timer needed 36 cycles, Prob140_fsm_hdlc needed 16 cycles). Increasing max_cycles gives the attacker more time to explore state spaces and reach the problematic conditions.
